item.title: Ordering at a café
item.context_text: You are on a trip to London. You are hungry, so you go into a small café. You read the menu and order your food.
item.objective_text: Read the menu, understand the waiter, and order one food and one drink.
item.target_grammar: Can I have…? / I'd like… for ordering
item.cultural_note: In British cafés people say "please" and "thank you" a lot. "Can I have a tea, please?" sounds friendly and normal.
success_conditions: Find prices and what comes with the food
Understand what the café does not have today
Order one food and one drink politely

children.title: Read the menu
children.instructions: Read the menu. Then answer the questions.
children.prompt_text:
CAFÉ MENU
Drinks: tea £2, coffee £3, orange juice £3
Food: chicken sandwich £6, vegetable soup £5, chocolate cake £4
The soup comes with bread.

questions.prompt: How much is the vegetable soup?

questions.explanation: The menu says "The soup comes with bread."

children.title: Listen to the waiter
children.instructions: The waiter comes to your table. Listen. Then answer the questions. You can listen again.
children.prompt_text: Hi there! Sorry, we have no chicken sandwiches today. But the soup is very good, and the chocolate cake is fresh. Sit down, and I can bring your food to your table.

questions.explanation: The waiter says "we have no chicken sandwiches today".

questions.prompt: What does the waiter say he can do?
options: Bring the food to your table
questions.explanation: He says "I can bring your food to your table."

children.title: Order your food
children.instructions: Order out loud. Ask for one food and one drink from the menu. Remember: there are no chicken sandwiches today.
children.prompt_text: Waiter: What can I get you?
children.goal: Order one food and one drink politely.
children.model_answer: Can I have the vegetable soup and a cup of tea, please?
